made.note: Batch 41 is bigger than last week: 94 files, nine concepts, 29 adsets, in three upload days. Wednesday for Latina, Local Dating English and Mature; Thursday for International Friend; Friday for Gringo, Passport Bro and the rest. So some adsets have five days of data, some only three.

scoreboard.title:
Last week refresh status:
4 worked, 8 almost, 1 watch, 6 worse, 9 missed
scoreboard.foot: Verdicts as on the rules slide. Early reads: final call at week 4 (week of 30 Nov). Next: one slide per refresh, biggest priority first, then its action items.
scoreboard.note: Nothing is final after three to five days. Four worked, eight almost, one to watch, six got worse and nine missed. We go in priority order, spend times how bad the read is: Passport Bro first, then Local Dating, International Friend, Latina, Gringo, Mature.

personas.title: Passport Bro Refresh: Dreamlife
personas.sub: Result: 1 almost, 1 missed · dreamlife is #3 on iOS with 15%
personas.foot: Before = 30 Oct – 5 Nov · After = 6–8 Nov (3 days: an early read) · rows: in top 3 first (best → worst), then the rest (worst → best)
personas.note: Dreamlife, the Gringo winner, went into Passport Bro on Friday. After three days it is third on iOS with 15 percent and ROAS went up to 0.37, still under the bar. On Android it got 6 percent and the adset slipped under 0.40.

actions.title: Passport Bro: bring back wanted, its 11-week #1, in a new form

rows.action: J2 · wanted’s “how life feels after marrying her”, new couple and kitchen. #1 here for 11 weeks, the longest reign.
Week 2: #3 on iOS at 0.55, adset 0.31 → 0.37.
0.42 → 0.39: the Batch 40 banner variants took 16% at 0.31. Combo (0.44) and boysvmen (0.45) held. Hold budget.

actions.foot: Why Android dipped (30 Oct – 5 Nov vs 6–8 Nov): the creatives. Not media buying ($754 → $796/day, nothing switched off), not the countries.
actions.note: Passport Bro's best run was wanted, eleven weeks at number one, so the next batch brings it back in a new form. Dreamlife stays on. Android dipped because the banner variants from last week took spend at a lower ROAS, not because of combo or the budget.

personas.title: Local Dating: Colosseum (EN), Talkinghead (ES)
personas.sub: Result: 1 worked, 1 almost, 2 got worse, 1 missed · colosseum lifts iOS EN, sinks Android EN
personas.foot: Before = 7 days before upload · After = upload – 8 Nov (EN from Wed 4 Nov, 5 days; ES from Fri 6 Nov, 3 days) · Android ES is a new adset (6 Nov)
personas.note: Colosseum 50/50 is the new concept from Teddy and Kim. On iOS it is second with 43 percent and the adset went up to 0.52. On both Android adsets it took 28 to 41 percent and ROAS dropped to 0.30 and 0.22. Same ads, opposite results by OS. Spanish got talkinghead variants, too small to count yet.

actions.title: Colosseum pays on iOS only: copy it to Spanish iOS, pull it from Android

rows.action: New visual, same message as both EN winners: “dating apps are a fight men lose” (datingcontest’s contest skit; colosseum’s 80 men vs 20 women). Both OS.
J1 · colosseum in Spanish, iOS only. It worked on iOS EN (🥈 43%, 0.44 → 0.52); datingcontest made the same EN → ES move and became #1 in both ES adsets.
Pause colosseum on both Android adsets: it hooks best (0.50) but its Android installers buy 6 per 100 vs datingcontest’s 14. Budget also rose 25% that week: hold it.
Loc. Dating EN · iOS: keep colosseum on (0.52). Android ES is a 3-day-old adset at 0.21: give it the week.

actions.foot: Purchases per 100 installs: colosseum 12 on iOS EN (datingcontest 17), 6 on the main Android EN adset (datingcontest 14). Not the countries. Messages from the ad names: to confirm with screenshots.
actions.note: Colosseum does the same job on both phones: it stops the thumb. On iOS the people who install go on to pay; on Android they pay half as often as datingcontest's. So it goes to Spanish on iOS only and comes off Android. English gets a new visual with the message both winners share.

personas.title: International Friend Refresh: Lipsync
personas.sub: Result: 3 missed · lipsync got under 1% in English
personas.foot: Before = 29 Oct – 4 Nov · After = 5–8 Nov (4 days) · 2 more lipsync files went to Friends ES under a Batch 45 label ($42): not counted
personas.note: Lipsync is new for International Friend, live since Thursday in English and Chinese. It barely got spend: under 1 percent in English, 6 percent in Chinese. Android English is still the problem at 0.31. iOS English is fine at 0.48 on banner.

actions.title: Friends: a new visual for tweetoverlay, the car-window banner for CH

rows.action: Same message, new visual: tweetoverlay has led Android EN and ES for 12 weeks (a tweet over a collage of friends from other countries: “Brazil, Italy, Korea friends”). Lipsync got under 1%.
New visual · the car-window banner, 3 new photos: #1 in CH (0.39) and in Friends EN iOS for 16 weeks (0.48).
J2: tweetoverlay led PT for 4 weeks before it faded. Bring it back in Portuguese with a new visual, then switch PT back on.
Last week’s pause is half done, and the internationalfriends ads still on now earn 0.35 (adset 0.31): keep them until next week’s read.
Friends EN · iOS: banner (car window) has led 16 weeks at 0.48.

actions.foot: Android EN rose 0.25 → 0.31 on tweetoverlay (0.30 → 0.34) and the internationalfriends ads still on (0.15 → 0.35), not on the batch. Ad-name read of tweetoverlay and the banner: to confirm with screenshots.
actions.note: Tweetoverlay has led International Friend for twelve weeks, so its message works; the visual is what's tired. The next English brief keeps the message and changes the visual. Portuguese gets tweetoverlay back. Chinese still needs its research.

personas.title: Latina Lover Refresh: Dancing + Sliders
personas.foot: Before = 28 Oct – 3 Nov · After = 4–8 Nov (5 days)
personas.note: Dancing variants and the new sliders went live on Wednesday. Dancing took number one in both English adsets within five days, about three quarters of spend, but ROAS stayed low: 0.31 on Android, 0.27 on iOS. In Portuguese the number one banner video had been switched off the day before; dancing took 46 percent at about the same ROAS. Spanish iOS is healthy on banner.

actions.title: Keep the dance, change the message; turn Portuguese’s #1 back on

rows.action: New angle · dancing’s opening (best hook, 0.33) with wanted’s “in a mood to talk”: 20 buyers per 100 installs vs dancing’s 6–9.
J2 · banner, #1 here for 14 weeks, with a new photo.
New angle · the new Latina EN set, in Spanish.
Turn the Argentina big-ticket video back on: 77% of spend at 0.30, off since 2 Nov. Dancing (0.29) didn’t sink PT.
Pause dancing: 76% of spend at 0.28; its installers buy half as often as banner’s.
Book the Latina call this week: three decisions in the next section.

actions.foot: Not the countries. PT’s strike is in question: its #1 ad was switched off the day before the batch landed.
actions.note: Dancing stops the thumb but doesn't bring payers, so English keeps the dance and changes what it says. Portuguese is different: its number one ad was switched off the day before dancing landed, and dancing actually did as well as that ad. So we turn it back on before we judge. And Latina gets its own call this week.

divider.title: Why Latina Lover is here
divider.text: It earned its place in July and August. Since September it has sat under the account. Three decisions for the call.
divider.note: Before the call, the whole story of Latina Lover: why we have it, where it still works, and what we need to decide.

slides.eyebrow: Latina Lover · all adsets, by month
slides.title: It beat the account by 13–16% in July and August; since September it’s under it
slides.foot: Meta ROAS, all after the Singular switch. Launched 27 Apr in English; Spanish and Portuguese from July. Since launch: $302k at 0.44 (account 0.42 over the same months).
slides.note: Latina started small in April in English. In July and August it beat the account by thirteen to sixteen percent and grew to eleven percent of all spend, mostly Spanish. Since September it has been under the account every month.

slides.eyebrow: Latina Lover · each adset, last 8 weeks
slides.title: It still works where one woman speaks to him: Spanish iOS and English Talk
rows: a woman behind a fence: “¿quieres venezolana?”
one woman’s selfie: “in a mood to talk”
“many Latinas want a man from another country”
a woman holding a big ticket to Argentina
slides.foot: 14 Sep – 8 Nov. Purchases per 100 installs: wanted “in a mood to talk” 20, banner 12, dancing 6–9. Messages read from the ad names.
slides.note: Where Latina still works, the ad is one woman speaking straight to him: the Spanish big-ticket banner and the English wanted selfie, both number one for months. The party and group ads bring viewers but not payers.

slides.title: For the call: three decisions on Latina

rows.action: Talk earns 0.44, Casual 0.28–0.34 (8 weeks). Move Casual’s budget into Talk, or keep testing Casual?
0.26 for 8 weeks, at 3 strikes. Turn its #1 back on and give it 2 weeks, or pause Portuguese?
The card says men who “feel they have no shot”. The payers answer one woman who wants to talk. Rewrite the card from the data?
This week, with the media buyer: bring the screenshots of banner and wanted, and where each idea came from.

slides.foot: After the call, the answers go into the Latina persona files (brain/minds/LatinaFemaleLover-*).
slides.note: Three things to decide on the call: whether English Casual keeps its budget, whether Portuguese stays, and whether we rewrite the persona card from what the data says about who pays.

personas.title: Gringo Lover Refresh: Flirted Too Hard + Lipsync
personas.sub: Result: 2 worked, 2 almost, 1 watch, 1 got worse, 3 missed · dreamlife took #1 in TH
personas.foot: Before = 30 Oct – 5 Nov · After = 6–8 Nov (3 days: an early read) · rows: in top 3 first (best → worst), then the rest (worst → best)
personas.note: Two new concepts for Gringo went live on Friday, flirtedtoohard and lipsync, plus dreamlife for Thailand. After three days, Philippines iOS and Spanish iOS worked, both up to about 0.53. Philippines Android got worse with the same ads. In Thailand dreamlife is already #1; ROAS came down from 0.72 but stays above 0.40, so we watch it. English barely took the new ads, and iOS English fell to 0.38.

actions.title: Gringo: more of the creator chat; pause PH Android

rows.action: New visual, same message · the creator chat “can I see your pictures… except on Bumpy”: 0.65 and 25 buyers per 100 installs on iOS EN (combo 0.44 and 12).
J1 · the creator myth-break “el amor de tu vida vive en otro país” (0.52 in Gringo ES), in Indonesian.
Keep the batch on in iOS ES and PH (0.53–0.55); watch TH (0.72 → 0.46).
Pause the batch on Android: dreamlife took 29% at 0.31, ROAS 0.42 → 0.36. Same batch worked on iOS PH (0.55).
Finish last week’s pause: the creator couple ads still lead (56%); their installers buy 4 per 100.

actions.foot: iOS EN fell 0.54 → 0.38 as combo (#1 for 6 weeks) dropped 0.51 → 0.30: not media, not the countries. Airport carries Android EN (0.40) and PT (0.60).
actions.note: Gringo had the most wins this week, in Spanish and Philippines iOS, so those ads stay on. English is the gap: the new ads didn't get spend and iOS English dropped, so English gets a new concept. Two media-buyer items, one of them still open from last week.

personas.title: Mature Dating Refresh: Banner
personas.sub: Result: 2 almost, 1 flat, 1 got worse · wanted still holds 94% of iOS EN
personas.foot: Before = 28 Oct – 3 Nov · After = 4–8 Nov (5 days) · all four are Mature 30to40 adsets
personas.note: Mature got 18 banner files on Wednesday, in English, Japanese and Korean. Wanted still owns iOS English with 94 percent, so banner can't move it. Android is flat at 0.30. Japan and Korea are far under the bar with or without banner: 0.19 and 0.07.

actions.title: Mature EN: a Linda twin with “serious relationship only”; cut KR

rows.action: New visual · a Linda twin: a woman in her 30s, beach selfie, name, age and city, “serious relationship only”, the line both Mature winners share.
0.19, wanted #1 for 14 weeks; the new banner did 0.47 at 19%: more banner, or less budget?
Cut: 0.07. Budget is already down 30% ($141 → $98/day) and wanted is off; banner leads at 0.13.

actions.foot: Linda (“Linda from Barcelona, 33, serious relationship only”) has led iOS 30–40 since June at 94%. manyplaces lifted 50–60 to 0.53 with “they only want a serious relationship”. August’s 8 new faces peaked at 4–34%.
actions.note: Yes, we refresh wanted, but history says how. Since June one ad, Linda from Barcelona, has carried 94 percent of iOS. In August we tried eight new faces, older women and men from other countries, and none beat her. So the new visual stays close to Linda: a woman in her thirties, a beach selfie, the same serious-relationship line.

personas.title: Sexy Female Lover Refresh: Wanted
personas.sub: Result: 1 worked · ROAS up to 0.73 in 3 days
personas.foot: Before = 30 Oct – 5 Nov · After = 6–8 Nov (3 days) · 4 of the files carry a Batch 42 label · Leave: keep the wanted variants on, re-read next week

followup.title: Batch 40 one week on: one more worked, most of it faded
points: Friends iOS EN moved from almost to worked: 0.44, with internationalfriends at 15%.
Gringo PH: dreamlife is still #1 (32%) at 0.40, so it stays on watch.
Everywhere else the Batch 40 ads fell to 0–14% of spend: Gringo and Local Dating moved on without them.

divider.title: Creator Creative as Ads
divider.text: No new creator batch this week. The 16 creator ads from Batch 44 (live Fri 30 Oct), read again after 10 days.
divider.note: No new creator content went live this week, so this section re-reads last week's creator ads with ten days of data.

creator.eyebrow: Live: Fri 30 Oct · 10 days of data
creator.sub: Top 3 in 6 of 12 adsets · #1 in Gringo ID and Loc. Dating Android ES · 1 worked, 2 got worse, 1 to watch
creator.foot: Before = 23–29 Oct · After = 30 Oct – 8 Nov · rows: creator in top 3 first (best → worst), then the rest (worst → best)
creator.note: Ten days in, creator ads are in the top 3 of six adsets and lead two of them. Only one is a clear win: Gringo Spanish Android, up from 0.22 to 0.46. Local Dating Spanish got worse on both OS, and in Gringo Indonesia the couple ads still lead at 0.26. Our own past winners still hold everything else.

actions.title: Creators who talk to camera bring payers; couple photos don’t

rows.action: Same message, new creator · “el amor de tu vida vive en otro país”, a myth-break to camera: hook 0.39, 4.1 s watched, 11 buyers per 100 installs (account video: 0.26, 2.7 s, 8).
Pause the creator couple ads: #1 at 61% since 30 Oct at 0.26; their installers buy 3–5 per 100. Asked last week.
The new adset is led by the creator talkinghead (48%) at 0.12: pause it if it is still under 0.20 after 7 days.
Loc. Dating ES · iOS: keep the creator talkinghead (0.62, 20 buyers per 100). ROAS fell because datingcontest (#1, 70%) dropped 0.50 → 0.31. Gringo EN · Android: creator ad #3 at 12%, 0.45: watch.

actions.foot: Creator ads, 30 Oct – 8 Nov. The talking-head ads that spent: hook 0.37–0.39, 4.1 s watched. Couple testimonials: hook 0.18–0.31, 2–3 s. Next: ask each creator where the idea came from.
actions.note: The creator lesson is clear now: creators talking straight to camera with a myth-breaking line hold attention and bring paying users; couple photo testimonials don't. So Gringo Spanish gets more of the myth-break, and the couple ads in Indonesia come off. Loc. Dating Spanish iOS isn't the creator's fault: datingcontest fell.

news2.title: 9 creatives jumped into the top 3; Slavic PT and ES fell hard
news2.foot: Sorted by ROAS after, then by biggest improvement · Before = week of 26 Oct · After = week of 2 Nov
news2.note: Nine creatives jumped into a top 3. Pickyourasian helped Asian Lover Android up to 0.42. On the other end, Slavic Portuguese fell as its two main creatives faded together, Slavic Spanish fell after standup was switched off, and Sexy Male fell to 0.13 after most of its ads were switched off.

actions.title: Two drops were switch-offs: log every one

rows.action: “They only want a serious relationship”: manyplaces took #1, 0.25 → 0.53. Linda’s line too: into the Mature EN brief.
J1 · wanted (0.87 in Slavic iOS EN), in Portuguese. Talkinghead and combo faded together.
Turn standup back on: 39% of spend, off since 3 Nov; ROAS 0.35 → 0.21.
Cut budget: 0.13. Ads with 69% of the spend were switched off; the rest runs at 0.04–0.13.
beatsyncedtext fell 1.04 → 0.38 in its first week as #1: no budget change yet.
About 40 ads were switched off on 6 Nov. Log every switch-off: date, ad, why.

actions.foot: Not the countries: in all but 4 adsets ROAS moved inside the same countries. Slavic iOS EN’s new #1 also followed a switch-off (2–3 Nov).
actions.note: Account news now comes with the why. Two of the biggest moves were switch-offs, not creatives: Slavic Spanish lost standup, Sexy Male lost most of its ads. Slavic Portuguese is a real creative fade, so it gets wanted from Slavic English. And manyplaces gives us the line for the Mature brief.

funnel.eyebrow: Worse and missed · where the new creative breaks
funnel.title: Five got the click but lost the install; three lost the click
funnel.foot: New creative · the other ads, same adset and days. CTR = link clicks per impression · C>I = installs per click · IPM = installs per 1k impressions · payers = purchases per 100 installs. Red = 20%+ worse. iOS installs per ad are Meta’s estimate.
funnel.note: For every set that got worse or missed, this is where the new creative lost. Five got people to click and then lost them before the install: that points at the store page not keeping the ad's promise, so those store pages get checked. Three lost the click itself, dancing among them: people watch, then scroll on. Three aren't a funnel problem at all.
